acceptance: The executor preamble's verify step tells the executor to run the verifier and test suite in the foreground and not to end its turn while a command it started is still running, because a headless worker turn ends when the agent replies and nothing resumes it when a background job finishes

docs/orchestration-workers.md names this failure (completion with READY missing after a reply that says a background run is still going) and the coordinator's recovery: worker message telling the executor to rerun in the foreground

role_prompt_rca.py stays under the 400-line cap; a test asserts the rendered executor prompt carries the foreground rule, and any pinned prompt text in the context regression set is updated rather than loosened
nodes.title: Executor prompt keeps long commands in the foreground so a headless turn does not end before its tests finish

acceptance: worker delegate, message and resume start the wrapper with the interpreter's safe-path flag (-P), so python -m specy_road.worker_runner run with cwd set to a worktree imports the package the launching CLI came from (the PYTHONPATH entry worker_runner already sets) and never the worktree's specy_road

A test spawns a worker whose worktree contains a specy_road/worker_runner.py that would fail on import, and shows the wrapper still runs, writes its log and records an exit; the test fails if -P is removed

The harness command the wrapper launches keeps its own environment unchanged (no PYTHONSAFEPATH or -P leaks into the executor's tests), shown by an assertion on the harness environment; worker_runner.py stays under the 400-line cap
nodes.title: The worker wrapper imports the launching specy-road, not the worktree's copy

acceptance: review-packet inlines diff text only up to a byte budget as well as the --max-diff-lines line budget (default about 200 KB, settable with --max-diff-bytes, 0 = no cap); files past either budget are listed with their +/- counts and byte size, and the full diff still goes to DIFF.patch

Files under a generated-artefact path (by default specy_road/pm_gantt_static/ and any path a .gitattributes line marks linguist-generated) are never inlined; the packet lists them with counts and size and says they are generated

Tests cover a diff of a few very long minified lines exceeding the byte budget and a generated-path file; docs/orchestration-review.md documents both rules; review_packet.py stays under its 400-line cap
nodes.title: The review packet caps its inlined diff by bytes too and lists generated bundles by size only

acceptance: review record writes REVIEW-<model>.md with that exact case even when a file differing only in case already exists (as on macOS APFS), replacing it rather than keeping the old name

handoff status, review list and the review gate find a reviewer record whose file name differs from REVIEW-<model>.md only in case, and report it under the canonical name; a test simulates the lowercase file
nodes.title: Review records are found and written with the canonical file name on case-insensitive filesystems

acceptance: The executor preamble's may-not list forbids pattern-based process kills (pkill, killall, kill by name or by a pgrep pattern) and allows stopping only a process the executor itself started, by the pid it recorded, because other sessions share the machine

docs/orchestration-workers.md records the failure (an executor's 'pkill -f "pytest -q"' ended the coordinator's and other leaves' test runs) in one or two lines and stays under its 400-line cap; a test asserts the rendered executor prompt carries the rule; role_prompt_rca.py stays under its cap
nodes.title: The executor prompt forbids killing processes the executor did not start

acceptance: Confirm from the installed Codex (and Cursor) model inventories whether GPT-6.1 Terra is available and under which id, recording the capture; if it is not available, write that down and stop

Run it as an executor on two or three small, already-landed Agentic-led leaves replayed from their base commit (no merges), recording usage, wall time, verifier outcome and the reviewers' verdicts on its result against the landed version
Write a short findings note under research/ with a recommendation (roster it as an executor, or not) for the maintainer; add a model profile only if the recommendation is yes

The pilot records the Codex CLI version it ran; if GPT-6.1 Terra is missing from the codex-cli 0.165.0 inventory, it is rechecked on 0.166.0 or later (the changelog adds Terra in 0.165/0.166) before the note says it is not available.
nodes.title: Pilot GPT-6.1 Terra as a lower-cost executor before rostering it
